ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Preventive Visit — Friedrich Nietzsche — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Mr. Nietzsche is a 36-year-old writer with chronic migraine on galcanezumab, recovering from medication overuse headache after a three-week taper of a butalbital combination, and with pathologic myopia of the right eye and a recent posterior vitreous detachment, who comes for his preventive visit two weeks after his four-week review. He has had headache on 4 days in the past two weeks, 2 of them with migraine features, treated with sumatriptan or naproxen. His second galcanezumab injection, given two weeks ago, caused only mild redness at the site. The floaters in his right eye are fading and he has had no new flashes. He sleeps about five and a half hours and has started the insomnia program. He has not had a tetanus booster for more than ten years and has never been tested for HIV or hepatitis. [S]

S — Synthetic diagnosis made at the consultation, anchored to his documented use of many medicines and sedatives; not a claim about his real medicines.
High myopia in both eyes, much worse in the right eye, since early childhood, with long-standing poor vision in the right eye and unequal pupils; comprehensive eye examination booked

Follow-up: Eight-week review in two weeks, with the third galcanezumab injection and the repeat dilated eye examination. HIV, hepatitis C and hepatitis B results by phone. Second hepatitis B vaccine dose in one month. Next preventive visit in one year. Next scheduled visit 1881-09-15: eight-week review of prevention: headache days, disability, mood, sleep and the plan ahead. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 16 minutes, with his consent. He named a health care agent, a close friend with whom he corresponds, and a health care proxy form was completed; the agent is recorded in the chart and is not named here. He said that what matters most to him is being able to think clearly, to read and write, and to walk. He chose not to record specific treatment preferences today. The plan will be revisited yearly or after any serious illness. [S]
